honest-review.summary: Two test cases, the same written checks for every setup. v1.1 passed **56 of 56 checks (100%)**, against 100% for v1.0, 68% for design-critique and 64% with no skill. design-critique only switched itself on in 2 of 4 runs.
changes: The verdict must start with one of three fixed labels: Ship, Ship after fixes or Rework.
Every finding needs all three labelled parts, with quoted evidence from the file.
Contrast is measured from the real colours and reported as a ratio.
The score block is always the last thing in the review, and em dashes are banned.
honest-review.method: Method: every setup ran each case in a clean Claude Code session with no other skills installed (`claude plugin eval`), and an independent model graded each run against the same written checks (three votes per check). Runs per setup across both cases: no skill 2, design-critique 4, v1.0 2, v1.1 8. The cases and checks are in the skill’s `evals/` folder on GitHub.

user-flow-creator.summary: Two test cases, the same written checks for every setup. v1.2 passed **21 of 24 checks (88%)**, against 42% for v1.0, 11% for ux-flow-designer and 50% with no skill.
changes: A ‘What changed’ list explains every removed or automated step.
Flows in money, health or identity products must show safeguards as stages.
Every flow lists its failure paths: lost messages, expired links, drop-offs, outages.

When it can't save a file, it pastes the complete HTML instead of a text outline, so the diagrams, table and edge cases survive. (The test sessions block file writing for every setup, which is why no setup passes ‘An HTML file is produced’.)
Flow rules borrowed from super-ux: every decision is a branch, every error lands on recovery, entry points listed, happy path of five stages or fewer.
A self-check list runs before the flow is handed over.
fixed: Demo request flow: An HTML file is produced. (0% → 50% of runs)
Demo request flow: The HTML contains at least two pipeline diagrams, one for the current flow and one for the improved flow. (0% → 100% of runs)
Demo request flow: Each pipeline has a label lozenge and an outcome title. (0% → 100% of runs)
Demo request flow: The HTML includes a step table with stage, actor and failure case columns. (0% → 100% of runs)
Demo request flow: The HTML lists edge cases or open questions. (0% → 100% of runs)
Password reset flow: Security is addressed for a banking context (e.g. identity verification, rate limiting, or notifying the user of the change). (0% → 100% of runs)
